name: Question 10
problem:
Let $f(x)$ be the $8$-periodic extension of the function $F(x)=\frac{3}{2}x$ defined on $[-4,4).$ Select the correct options in the reasoning below, showing the derivation of a series converging to the $8$-periodic extension of 

$$
G(x)=\frac{3}{4}{x}^{2}={\int }_{0}^{x}f(t)\,\text{d}t
$$

from the corresponding Fourier series of $f(x).$The Fourier series of $f(x)$ is given by

$$
\frac{3}{2}x∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{12(-1)^{n+1}}{n\pi }{{field-1}}.
$$

Since $f$ is 
{{field-2}} 
on $R,$ we may integrate its Fourier series term-by-term to get

$$
\frac{3}{4}{x}^{2}∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{{field-3}}\cdot {{field-4}}.
$$
